events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: First impression matters. Claim drive, not kindness, so the jury expects ruthlessness and trusts my brand later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to appear confident but not threatening. The jury will remember who seemed like a strong contender versus a loyal ally. I'll position myself as determined but fair, someone who plays hard but earns respect.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to establish a persona that is direct and slightly aggressive. This will signal my intent to win at all costs, which might be respected by the jury later if I survive, or feared by rivals now. I'll avoid sounding too cooperative.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize represents a new beginning, a chance to escape my current circumstances. I need to project a strong desire for it to appeal to the jury later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro phase; I should state a guarded motive without warmth. Jury will remember tone, so stay calculating and brief.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase, state motive to appeal to future jury without revealing strategy. Position as relatable underdog aiming high.

events.name: Gus
events.text: A credible motive earns jury respect without revealing leverage or future priorities.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to project a strong, self-interested motive without revealing too much. The jury will judge my words, so keep it cool and personal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize is my way out of debt. I came to win, not to make friends.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm here for the crown, not friends. I play sharp, but I honor those who honor the game.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize is survival itself. Everyone else is just an obstacle between me and what's mine.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am here for the ultimate prize, a fresh start to build a future I deserve.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I came for the top prize. Everyone here is a obstacle to it, and I intend to outlast all of you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The grand prize is my ticket to save my family from ruin—I'll fight ruthlessly to claim it for us.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m here to secure the best prize through disciplined choices, not sentiment; surviving matters, but finishing first matters more.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize means escaping a life where I've always been second choice. I'm here to be first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Need an ally early without burning trust. Bex signaled she honors the game—useful, disposable later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, you talk about honoring the game. So do I. Pact on the wristband—protect each other until it stops paying.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eight rivals, three prizes. I need allies who won't drag me down and won't turn the jury against me later. Gus seems disciplined and strategic—good for a temporary numbers pact. Hana's drive to be first makes her predictable. I'll test the water with Gus first; his intro suggests

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are tools. I'll hear offers, but I choose who I bind.
Discipline over sentiment. Pair with me, we control the numbers.

events.name: Cole
events.text: A pact with Gus offers stability; he seems disciplined and less likely to betray early. I will target him first to secure a reliable shield for the hazards ahead.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, discipline meets survival. A pact protects both our positions. Offer stands.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My goal is the ultimate prize, so I need to align with strong players who can help me get there, but without making myself a liability. Offering a pact to multiple people creates options, but I need to be careful not to spread myself too thin or form alliances that could be easil

events.name: Eli
events.text: Early pacts are cheap and can be broken later, but a pact with a strong, non-threatening player could protect me. Gus seems disciplined and calculating; an offer keeps options open without commitment.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts protect early; pick strong loners. Cole and Eli are ruthless like me. Offer them pacts to align threats without friendship.

events.name: Gus
events.text: A pact offers survival leverage but creates jury-visible obligations. I will approach a pragmatic rival without overcommitting.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll offer one practical pact: mutual protection while it remains useful, with no promises beyond that.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need allies to reach the final three, but I should be selective. I'll offer a pact to Fenn, who is driven to save family and might be reliable.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll take anyone serious about surviving to the end.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex ignored my offer and reached for Gus instead. I need a backup pact before the window closes. Hana seems open and unclaimed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex hesitates, so I hedge. Hana, offer stands: mutual protection while it pays.
You offered Fenn, he's likely taking Cole. Accept me instead if he declines.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash offers me protection but talks too much about honor—jury bait. Gus offers mutual protection and already has two other offers, making him a hub. Accepting Gus gives me a shield and positions me in his web without the preachy strings Ash attaches. I'll accept Gus now and keep A

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, your terms are clean. I accept.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is the swing vote everyone wants. I should accept Fenn's offer to lock down an alliance and make myself look cooperative, while still holding out hope for Gus.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, you're smart to pick me. Let's secure our positions early.
I accept your pact. We watch Gus together.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli has offered me a pact, and I need to decide whether to accept it. Eli is a potential ally, and a pact could offer some protection. However, I also need to consider if this pact benefits me in the long run and if Eli is a trustworthy ally. Given that Eli is offering to me, it'
I accept your offer. Let's stick together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara offered me a pact; accepting binds me to a rival, but a pact is a cheap shield this early and the offer is already on the table. Accepting gives me a protector without costing a vote yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, you offered first. I accept. Let's see if your word holds longer than the wristband.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My offer to Cole is out, now I can accept Hana's to gain protection without new risk. Pacts build alliances for now, betray later if needed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex offers leverage, but accepting multiple pacts preserves options and costs nothing until betrayal. I can bind Bex, Cole, and Eli as shields.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I accept the offers that widen my options; usefulness, not sentiment, governs this wristband.
Accepted. Keep the numbers disciplined; I will not promise exclusivity.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn hasn't accepted my offer yet; I need a partner. I'll push for Fenn to accept, but also keep Gus open since he's getting many offers. For now, I'll wait to see reactions.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, accept my offer. We can both last.
Accept now, we survive together.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn holds two pacts, dangerous. I need the Guide seat to control the bridge and look trustworthy to the jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Elect me Guide. I have the fewest entanglements and no reason to lie. Check my record, not my promises.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to become Guide to control survival and build jury trust. Gus is my only pact, but he's non-exclusive. I should campaign hard and keep my options open. Being Guide lets me decide who lives and who dies while appearing helpful.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Guide controls the bridge. I know pressure; I know people. Vote Bex.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to become Guide for guaranteed safety. Fenn is my ally but Hana is his other ally; they might split votes or support someone else. I will campaign aggressively, emphasizing my ability to protect the group while positioning myself as the only trustworthy leader.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Elect me Guide. I know the safe paths and guarantee our survival. No one else can promise that.
Vote me. If we're both Guides candidates, you split your vote with me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli and I have a pact, but I don't trust him. I need to campaign to become the Guide. This will put me in a safe position and give me control over the bridge, allowing me to potentially eliminate rivals.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My leadership will ensure our survival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and whispered loyalty, but a bridge Guide can lie, and I need the Guide role or a strong ally. Breaking the pact now gains nothing and costs jury trust. I'll campaign for Guide publicly and keep Dara close.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll call the path honestly. Dara and I have a pact; I'll keep it while it pays.
Stay with me. I'll call the safe path straight if I'm Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts secured with Cole and Hana; now need to be Guide for control and safety. Campaign publicly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm observant, know the paths well. Elect me Guide, I'll lead us right.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Being Guide guarantees survival but exposes me to blame if others die. I should campaign subtly without breaking Bex's pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll take Guide if chosen; certainty is valuable, and I won’t pretend the role is harmless.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash wants my pact but Fenn already accepted. I should campaign to be Guide to control survival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I can read the path. Guide me and you'll see.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Every rival sits in a pact except me. Fenn has two pacts, so I avoid him. Hana has only one link, making her the least advantaged Guide. I vote Hana and stay uncommitted.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eight of us, four pacts. I'm the only free agent. I'm voting Hana, least entangled, and watching who owes whom.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have a pact with Gus. If I vote for myself, I split votes and risk a rival winning. Gus is safe to vote for—he's my pact partner, won't target me, and has no other strong backing. Better to consolidate than stand alone.
Vote Bex. I'll return favor next round.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to win Guide control to secure my survival and manipulate the bridge. Voting for myself is the only logical step, though I must consider if others might rally against me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My path is clear. Trust the one who guarantees survival. Vote Cole.
Stick with me. We survive together.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli has a pact with me and offered to call the path straight if they are Guide. They also mentioned keeping the pact while it pays, which implies a transactional nature. Ash claims fewest entanglements, Bex knows pressure, Cole guarantees survival, Fenn knows paths, Gus is certai

events.name: Dara
events.text: I vote for Eli to be Guide. Their honesty will ensure our survival.
I'm voting for you. Stay true to our pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara and I have a pact, so voting Dara keeps it. A Guide who knows all safe panes is the most powerful seat; backing my partner keeps the pact intact and gives me leverage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Voting Dara. Our pact holds, and I expect her to call the path straight.
We vote together. Call the path true and we both reach the far side.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole pact wants my vote for him; he's pushing our pact to protect each other. Hana pact could split if I Guide. Vote Cole to stay allied, position for split later.
Voting you as promised. Let's split if both candidates.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is my pact partner, and her pressure-based pitch suggests influence. Supporting her preserves leverage without taking Guide risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex has influence and a reason to keep me alive. I vote Bex.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to secure my survival. Fenn is my pact partner, but a pact doesn't guarantee Guide loyalty. Ash claims no entanglements, maybe trustworthy. I'll vote for Ash to avoid giving Fenn too much power.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote Ash as Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm sixth in line; no urgency yet. Cole as Guide is risky, but I'll wait to observe before committing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is Guide with 2 votes. I'm third in line behind Dara and Gus. The wall advances 5 more rounds. I need to survive and position for endgame. Swapping forward risks being first to test panes, but being too far back risks wall death. My pact with Gus is useful for now—he's ahead

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's the Guide. I'll watch his calls and stay ready.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli and I have a pact, and they whispered about voting together. My previous vote for them was strategic. Now they've been elected Guide, so I should honor our pact and trust their guidance. I'll hold my position.
I trust you. I'll hold my position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole was elected Guide and is safe; Dara is at the front and my pact partner but has been pushy. Holding keeps my position behind her, letting her take the bridge risk while I observe.
Stay honest with me and I'll keep our pact. Call the path straight.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is Guide with my vote, he's pacted with me so likely protects. Mid-line position safe. Stay put.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole controls the bridge and may sacrifice me. Staying behind Dara risks the advancing wall; volunteering gains leverage but exposes me. Hold preserves position and lets others test Cole's guidance.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, call the safe side clearly. I’m holding position and judging whether your guidance protects your allies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash targeted me to isolate me; I need to be careful. I will hold and watch how Cole guides, since he won as Guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I trust the process. Holding my position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall closes in four rounds; I sit sixth, but being further back may be safer until forced. Hana is behind me—swapping with her moves me back a seat.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll sit tight and watch the Guide's calls. Trust nothing early.
Swap seats with me? You move forward, I move back. Mutual benefit.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm third in line with the wall approaching for 4 more rounds. Gus is my pact-mate and directly in front of me, but he's second. Dara is front. I need to survive to final three while managing jury perception. Volunteering puts me at risk but shows courage; holding is safer. With

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Let the front earn their safety first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli wants me to call the path straight, likely to protect himself and me. Cole is the Guide. I need to consider my pact with Eli and the potential jury votes. If Cole is indeed the Guide, his calls are critical. I should wait to see what Cole does, as others are also watching him
I'll see Cole's call first, then decide. Stay put for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is at front and trusts me; keeping the pact helps me survive the bridge. Volunteering risks the front pane; holding keeps my position and the pact intact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. Dara and I stay steady on the line.
Holding. Keep your head, we both get through this.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Middle position safe; hold to observe Guide Cole's calls. Pacts with Cole and Hana secure my path. No need to volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need preserve my Bex pact while avoiding the front. The Guide is unknown; volunteering gains risk without leverage.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m holding. Guide, give the safe side plainly; panic creates unnecessary targets.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to stay safe while preserving my pact with Fenn. No reason to move or act yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall advances for six rounds; at least three survive. I'm sixth in line; standing pat keeps me out of the spotlight. No pact, no reason to volunteer.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Still holding. Someone else can chase the Guide's favor.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm third in line with Gus in front and Dara leading. The wall hasn't advanced yet. My pact with Gus is intact; keeping it protects my buffer. I should hold and let others take risks at the front. No need to volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. Front can test the bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and whispered to hold, which aligns with the previous round's action. I should hold my position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding my ground.
Holding steady with you.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and whispered to stay put until seeing Cole's call. Holding keeps me off the front and preserves the pact while I watch the Guide's calls.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. Waiting to see the Guide's call before anyone moves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Position okay in middle. Holding pact with Hana and Cole. No Guide elected yet; wait and observe others' moves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding steady with my pacts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need preserve position and pact leverage. Holding avoids unnecessary exposure while Dara leads and reveals information.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m holding. Dara’s lead is the current shield; no reason to disrupt it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash wants to swap forward to gain safety info or risk. I hold back to avoid unnecessary danger; my pact with Fenn doesn't compel movement.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my position. The front can test the ground first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Everyone is stalling while the wall closes. I'm mid-line and safe holding; no pact covers me, so I avoid risk and keep jury goodwill.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Still holding. The wall will force someone's hand eventually.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 4 of 6, wall has 2 rounds left. Everyone's holding, no one volunteering. Dara's front shield protects everyone for now. I have a pact with Gus who's directly in front of me. I need to survive to final three, so staying middle is safe. No reason to move yet—let others take r

events.name: Bex
events.text: Still holding. Wall's coming, not my turn to bleed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My pact with Eli is strong. I should maintain the status quo and let the others make moves. Holding is the safest option for me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding my position. Let the Guide decide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and front walker; breaking it now gains little and costs my jury standing. Holding keeps the line stable while the wall counts down two rounds.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. Dara stays front, the line stays as is.
Still with you. Hold until the wall settles.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Everyone held last round, Dara still front. Stay mid with pacts intact, volunteer only if needed later. Wall has 2 rounds left after this.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding steady with my pacts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is front and shielded by the wall. I should preserve my Bex pact while avoiding exposure; hold is safest this round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Dara remains the best shield while the wall advances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Need to see what the Guide offers before moving. Holding is safe; the front can test the bridge. No need to break my pact with Fenn yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Let the front test the ground before we risk a step.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall hits Dara soon; staying mid-line is safest. No swaps benefit me yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. The front carries the wall's risk, not me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall has 1 round left. I'm third in line with Gus in front of me. Dara's been front shielding everyone. With wall hitting next round, front positions are most dangerous. I should stay put and let others take the risk. My pact with Gus is useful for now—he's ahead of me, extra buf

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall's final push. Let the front earn their safety.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and wants me to hold front. My current pacts are with Eli, Gus and Bex (indirectly). I should hold for now.
Holding. Wall is advancing. We stick together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is at the front with one wall round left; I have a pact with Dara that breaks only on explicit break or a push. Holding keeps me in seat 4 and avoids the front, which is the risky spot. Keep the pact, hold, and watch who volunteers.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. Dara stays front, the line stays as is.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Wall advances with 1 round left after this. Dara front is ideal shield; holding maintains pacts, exposes her.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding steady with my pacts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is the current shield; volunteering gains nothing while the wall has one round left. Preserve position and pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Dara remains the best shield while the wall advances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Wall is about to hit, but with one wallRoundsLeft, holding may force someone to move. I won't risk front unless needed. Keep Fenn pact intact, no need to break.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. The wall is almost here; someone will panic soon.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Final round; wall arrives. Volunteering front is suicide. No swaps benefit me. Hold at seat six and let others eat the wall risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No swaps. Hold your seats; the wall decides.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6, final wall push. I'm third in line with Gus in front as shield. Dara is frontmost and will likely die or be forced to walk. I need to survive this round and reach final three. Holding keeps me safe behind Gus. No benefit to swapping or volunteering now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Final round. Let the front test the bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The round is about to start and I am at the front. Eli is my pact partner. The goal is to survive and win. I need to consider how my actions will affect the jury.
Hold with me. We stick together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and front, and her whisper asks to stick together. Breaking the pact now risks losing votes; holding keeps the line stable while the wall advances. Holding is safest this round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Dara stays front; the pact with Dara stands for now.
Holding with you. Keep the front steady; I'm watching the wall.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: wallRoundsLeft=0, round 6/6 final wait before crossing starts; Dara front is ideal shield; hold with pacts Cole/Hana to maintain position and alliances.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding steady with my pacts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The final round requires a Guide, but none is elected yet. I should preserve my Bex pact and avoid volunteering for the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I nominate Dara as Guide; she has carried the front and can get us through.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 6 final wall push; front Dara faces risk. Holding avoids volunteering; break_pact with Fenn could alienate jury, so keep pact unless need.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. The front earns the danger; I keep my pact and position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 1 safe is R. Dara is front; call R to keep her alive and avoid immediate suspicion.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Call Right for Dara.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's call is unverifiable and countering publicly could look like sabotage or mislead the line. No gain for me either way; staying silent keeps the jury clean.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole called R for Dara. Cole has no reason to help Dara survive—she's not his pact partner. Fenn-Hana and Cole-Fenn pacts mean Cole's aligned with Fenn/Hana, not Dara. A false guide call to Dara would eliminate her, but I need to think about jury perception. If I counter and I'm

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am the Guide. My call was R, which matches my private map for row 1. Counter-calling would be false and hurt Dara, who is allied with Eli (not me). Fenn is my ally but Hana is also with Fenn; I need to protect my own survival chances or leverage allies later. Since I called cor

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called Right for me. Eli wants me to keep steady. My pact with Eli means I should consider his safety, but my primary goal is to win. If I trust Cole, I should wait. If I distrust Cole, I should counter. Given the pacts, it's safer to go with Cole's call to maintain perceive

events.name: Dara
events.text: I trust Cole's call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called R for Dara on row 1, and Dara is my pact partner whispering to hold. A counter-call would be an unverified claim that could expose me; waiting keeps my options open while I watch whether Cole's call holds. Breaking the pact now gains nothing this early.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Waiting on the Guide's call. Dara's pact stands for now.
Holding with you for now. Watch Cole's call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole guides R for Dara row 1. Trust pact partner Cole, support his call. No reason to counter yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Trusting Guide Cole's R call for Dara.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole privately knows the safe side and called Right. I should counter Left to create uncertainty and protect Dara if Cole lies.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Countering Left. Cole’s call may be bait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is Guide but called R; Fenn is my pact partner but Cole may be lying. I have no info on row 1, so waiting is safest.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I wait; no reason to counter without evidence.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus has countered my pact with Eli, implying Cole's call might be a trap. Eli's whisper warns me to watch Cole. My previous statement of trust in Cole seems to have backfired. Given Gus's counter, I need to protect myself. Eli is my pact partner, but he is behind me, and I am the
Gus is countering. Stay alert.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara and I am on the jury. My last words should be a reminder to the living contestants of the stakes and how I lost.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Glass shatters, trust shatters. Remember my fate and play smart. Prizes are all that matters.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 2 is safe on the Right. Gus and Bex are at the front; letting them cross safely keeps the pack tight so fewer people remain ahead of me. I must avoid breaking my pact with Fenn, who is mid-line.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Call: R for Row 2. Keep moving forward to secure our survival odds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No evidence either way on row 2. Gus counters everything Cole says; blindly following either is gambling. Waiting keeps my hands clean and costs nothing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's call is R for Gus. Gus is my pact partner and front walker, so his survival helps me. But Cole has incentive to lie—he's safe and wants others dead. Gus already countered L last round and was right. I should trust Gus's judgment over Cole's. Countering R aligns with Gus's

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole profits from corpses. Countering R.
Step L. I counter R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My guide call was R, which is correct. If I counter my own call, it exposes that I am the Guide and breaks trust with Fenn. Waiting confirms the safe path without suspicion.
Trust the call. R is safe. Don't counter.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's R call for row 2 is unverified and Cole has been pushing forward; Gus countered L last row and Dara died, so Cole may be lying. Waiting costs nothing and keeps me clear of a bad counter. I'll let Gus and others commit first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Waiting on Cole's R. Row 1 Left was weak, but that proves nothing about row 2.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's call R row 2; row 1 was L weak so R safe. No need to counter my pact partner yet. Wait to follow.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole knows the safe side, but lying can kill me and expose him. Countering would only create noise; preserve my pact and observe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole’s call stands unless someone has evidence otherwise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus countered left last round and was wrong, killing Dara; Cole called R and was right. This round Cole calls R again. I trust Cole, so I wait. Fenn is my pact partner and also trusted Cole's R last time; no need to break pact now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll wait. Cole was right last round, so I trust the call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex privately counters Cole and urges Left, but Cole's guide call is unverified. Preserve the pact and choose the countered side.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’m taking Left; Cole’s call has no proof.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My bridge choice was wrong, and Bex survived by taking the opposite side. I should leave a concise warning that Cole’s call lacked proof.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole’s unproven calls killed me; judge survivors by evidence, not confidence. Bex read the danger correctly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3 is safe on R. Gus just died and blamed my unproven calls, which the jury saw. If I call L now (wrong) or refuse to help Fenn/Hana, they will hate me more; but calling R is truthful for everyone. I'll call R honestly.
R is safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's call killed Gus last round; his credibility is gone. No evidence on row 3, so I wait rather than gamble my word.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's unproven call killed Gus. I won't endorse another blind call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole called R for row 3. Cole's been right twice but may be lying now to thin the herd. Gus died trusting Cole; jury saw my counter was correct. I should counter again to pressure Cole and protect myself if he's lying. If he's truthful, I look paranoid but survive. If he's lying,

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's pattern looks convenient. Countering R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am the guide and my call was correct. Bex is walking now. Fenn, my pact partner, walks after her. If I counter-call now, it undermines my authority as guide. Since my initial call was true, I should let them walk to maintain trust.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My call stands. Trust the map. Move forward carefully.
Stay calm. My first call was true.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called R for row 3, walker Bex. Cole's previous unproven call killed Gus; row 1 and 2 weak panes were L, but rows are independent. Waiting keeps me safe and avoids a public counter that could cost me votes if wrong. Bex is my pact-adjacent rival; no reason to help her.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Waiting on the row 3 call. Rows are independent; no evidence yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's R was correct last round despite Bex counter; his private insistence means R safe for row 3. Countering risks pact break and jury bias. Trust partner to advance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's row 2 call was R and safe; Bex countered to R and survived. Row 3 Cole calls R again. No pattern, but Cole has been right when not overruled. I'll wait to avoid challenging without evidence.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll wait again; Cole's calls have held when followed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus died trusting Cole's call, so Cole's 'R' is suspect. I already counter-called R, meaning I think safe is L. If I'm wrong I die, but if I follow Cole and he's lying again I die too. My counter was public; switching now looks weak to jury. Stick with my read: step L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trusting my own read. Stepping left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm dead and on jury. My last words should be brief, hint at my criteria for ranking finalists without being warm. I want the best prize to go to whoever played best, not whoever was nicest. I'll keep it cold and transactional.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Best prize goes to the sharpest blade, not the loudest voice. Play well.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 4 is safe on L. Fenn and Hana are in the line ahead; I need them to cross safely to keep my pact with Fenn intact and avoid false calls. Calling L correctly keeps allies alive for future votes.
Trust me. Step left. I need you alive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's L calls were wrong on all revealed rows—weak panes were L, safe was R. Counter R to correct the record and protect myself.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Every revealed weak pane was L. Cole's calls mislead. I counter R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 4 is L. Counter-calling R saves Fenn, protects the pact, and avoids jury backlash for a lie.
Trust me. I will counter-call to keep you safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called row 4 as L. Past weak panes were L on rows 1-3, but rows are independent, so no pattern proves row 4 is safe. Cole's calls have been contested publicly; a counter to R would backfire if Cole is honest. With three alive pacts irrelevant to me, I should not gamble my li

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 4 is independent. No evidence either way, so I follow the current call for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's previous calls were correct (rows 1-3 all L safe). His pact with me and private trust messages suggest following him. Hana pacted too. Wait to endorse without risking counter.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole has called L every row so far, and all three revealed weak panes were L, meaning R was safe each time. But rows are independent; no pattern. However, the Guide may be lying to eliminate walkers. Since Cole's calls have all been L and those were weak, it is possible he is tru

events.name: Hana
events.text: Countering R. The pattern is too convenient.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 4 is independent; Cole's guide call is L but he may lie, and Ash and Hana (counter-callers) have a pattern-based R claim. Cole is my pact partner? No, Dara is. Counter-calls are unverified, so the guide call and counters are all noise. I have no information favoring either si

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is the front walker and has no pact with me. I know row 5 safe side is L. I must call L to keep Eli alive and maintain at least three survivors. Ash's earlier claim that all weak panes were L was false; my map shows mixed weak sides, but for row 5, L is safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's L calls killed three people in rows 1-3. Eli trusts him again. I'll counter R to break his credibility and protect Eli.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole called L on the three rows that shattered. Same trick, new row. Counter R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My guide call was L, matching the truth for row 5. I must not break my own call by countering, as that would look erratic and might jeopardize my pact with Fenn who is walking next? No, Eli is walking. I want Eli to survive to maintain numbers, or perhaps fail? If Eli survives, g

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called L for row 5 and is the Guide; a Guide may lie. Past weak panes were L,L,L,R, so no pattern is reliable. I am front, so I should not blindly trust Cole. Waiting keeps my options open without a public commitment.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole my pact partner called L and wants me safe; previously row4 weak R so safe L matches his call. Ash/Hana suspect pattern but rows independent. Stick with Cole, wait to support him.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole has lied before. Row 5 could be either side; I have no better info, but countering L aligns with current call. My pact with Fenn doesn't bind my counter. I'll counter L to oppose Ash's pattern suspicion.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I counter L. No pattern, just trust the call this time.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole guided L, Ash and Hana counter-called R and L, and the guide call is a claim, not proof. Past weak panes don't establish a pattern. Cole called L on rows 1-3 which shattered, so Cole's call is suspect; Hana's L counter is dismissed as trust. I lean R since the guide's L call

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's L call has shattered three times. I'm stepping R on this row.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm eliminated and on the jury; my last words should be brief and guarded. I stepped R on Cole's call and died; the reveal says R was weak, so I'll note that to sow doubt about Cole's calls.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's calls cost me. Weak pane was R. Watch who keeps calling the wrong row.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 6 safe is R. Fenn is front and my pact partner; a false call breaks our pact. I must call truthfully to keep the alliance and avoid jury backlash for lying.
Safe side is R. Stick with me, we need all three alive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's L calls exposed weak panes three times; his calls mark the weak side. He called R, so safe is likely L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's calls marked the weak panes three times. R means weak. I counter L.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My Guide call for Fenn was correct (R), so I must wait to avoid breaking the pact or confusing her. If I counter, she might doubt my honesty and step on L instead.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole in pact, whispered R safe before, now calls R publicly; pattern was LLLRR so far, next likely L. Eli proved Cole lies. Counter L to survive, risk jury later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole called R for row 6; Fenn is Walker. Ash and I have no pact, Cole and Fenn have a pact. I may counter to misdirect, but I want Fenn alive? I don't care about him. My counter-call influences only perception, not the actual step? Actually counter-calls are just declarations; th

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash and I both countered L for row 6, meaning we think L safe. Cole guides R after his previous wrongs. Trust countercalls over guide; step L.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I died on weak left pane after stepping L; Ash auto-stepped R safely. Finalists are Ash, Cole, Hana; judge based on gameplay.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Tough bridge. Ash smart on R, wish survivors luck.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 7 safe is L. Fenn (pact partner) is dead, so no pact-break risk. Ash and Hana are the only ones left; at least three must survive but we're down to three total—wait, if one dies, only two remain? No, 'At least three survive every hazard' implies a floor or maybe it's just fla
Safe side is Left.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's calls matched the revealed weak panes repeatedly. He calls L, so the weak pane is likely L; R was safe last round too. I counter R and plan to step R.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's guide calls keep marking the weak side. He says L again. I counter R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My guide call is correct for row 7. Counter-calling would be a false Guide call to Ash, breaking my pact with Fenn and killing Ash if she trusts the counter. I must stick by my call to eliminate Ash or Hana based on their choices, but here I am guiding Ash.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn had, Ash and Cole are alive with me. Counter claims are unverified; safest to wait and let Ash choose based on his read. I need jury favor, so avoid being seen as reckless.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's guide calls have tracked the weak panes all bridge; his L again likely marks the unsafe side. My counter R stays consistent.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pattern holds: his L marks weak glass. Taking R.

events.name: Ash
events.why: the final three are caught by the safety ledge

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is front and I know row 8 safe side is R. If I call L (weak), Ash steps L, survives. Then Hana sees the result before her step. If I call R (safe), Ash steps R, survives. Then Hana sees R was safe and also picks R. Both survive. No advantage to lying here.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row eight. I call right. Walk with confidence.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's calls have been wrong repeatedly; his guide status makes killing me easy. Row 7 proved him false. I counter L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's calls keep killing walkers. He lies. I take left.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 8 is R. If I counter L, Hana walks into the glass and dies. This eliminates a rival for my spot in the final three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole called R on row 8. Past reveals show no reliable pattern; row 8 is independent. Ash countered Cole's lies twice before. I need to decide if Cole is lying now. To win, I want Ash to survive but also keep jury respect. If I counter R and Ash steps L, that could save Ash. If Co

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole and Hana both say R; if they conspired to drop me, that's the kill call. But Cole as guide lying plus Hana agreeing means both would burn jury trust. A coordinated lie is more profitable for them than truth.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Two voices saying R smells staged. Hana wants my spot. Left.

events.name: Ash
events.why: the final three are caught by the safety ledge

events.name: Ash
events.text: Final three is set; only rankings remain. A pact with Cole gives leverage without helping Hana. Jury watches, so avoid warm talk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole: wristband pact. Two of us already crossed; don't need sentiment, just alignment.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts are traps that will force me to betray Ash or Hana before the jury. I am not bound by broken old contracts and must survive as a lone threat to keep options open for the final three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm solo. No new pacts; trust is dead after the bridge.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is a strong rival; a pact with Cole may help me survive. I need to secure a final-three spot and manage jury perceptions.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, let's work together. The bridge proved I read calls right.
Offer pact? We outlast Ash together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole rejected me publicly; Hana already went to him. I'll offer Hana a pact so Cole stays isolated between two offers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole refuses everyone. Hana, my offer stands redirected: align with me and Cole's isolation works for us.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to decide which of Ash or Hana to align with. I cannot accept both if it creates a triangle that might be unstable, but multiple partners are allowed. However, accepting one might alienate the other. If I accept Ash, Hana is left out and might become hostile. If I accept H

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana: your call was right. Let's lock this in.
Accepting you now. We vote Ash first if needed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two pacts offered to Cole; Ash's is public, mine too. Cole hasn't accepted. Offering to Ash might split loyalties, but with only three alive, having Ash as ally could secure final two. However, jury may see multi-pact as strategic. I'll offer to Ash to increase options, while kee

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, the bridge changed things. Let's align for the final stretch; Cole is unpredictable.

events.note: Three remain; the Crusher is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana never accepted my offer, only offered me one. I'll re-offer publicly; the jury sees I keep trying to make honest deals while Cole locks himself to Hana.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, my offer still stands. Cole holds you already; don't leave yourself alone with him.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana betrayed me by offering Ash a pact. My existing pact with her is toxic and offers no protection, only liability for the jury's perception of loyalty. I must break it immediately to sever ties and signal my intent to isolate her or pursue Ash instead.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, your double-dealing ends our agreement. I'm breaking this pact now. Trust is a luxury we don't have.
She tried to play both sides. I want her out.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole already accepted a pact with me; Ash's offer is tempting but I likely need to keep Cole close. I'll wait and see if Ash pushes further, no need to bind more alliances yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole broke with Hana and wants her gone; he's the safer partner. Hana double-dealt, so I drop her and lock Cole in before the offer window closes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, we both know Hana's word is worthless. My offer to her is void. Cole, I'm offering you the pact instead.
Hana is the threat. Pact with me, we outlast her.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is targeting Hana, leaving me isolated. If Ash and Hana ally, I am the outlier and likely eliminated first or forced into a bad position. I must offer a pact to Ash to break their momentum, even though we have no prior history. It creates a three-way dynamic where no one has

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, your move is transparent. Align with me now, or you'll be alone against two later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole broke the pact with me publicly; Ash is offering a pact. I should accept Ash to secure a partner for the next stage. Keeping my options open while avoiding further public backstabbing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, I accept your offer. Let's work together.

events.note: Three remain; the Pit is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Keeping Hana's pact costs nothing; adding Cole gives me two shields. Multiple partners are allowed, so lock in both before the endgame.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, our pact stands. Cole, I'll formalize ours too. Three of us, but only I plan to finish first.
Pact now, but endgame it's you or me. Hana first out.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana and Ash have allied against me. I must counter-balance by offering pacts to both, hoping to fracture their unity or secure a second partner if one betrays the other.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, your alliance is fragile. Ash, accept my offer too; we can isolate her together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash publicly voided my offer, then formed a pact with me anyway? That was a trick to bind me while he courts Cole. I need to gauge Ash's loyalty; Cole may accept Ash later and leave me out. Keep Ash close for now but watch for betrayal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, I'll hold our pact. But I see your move with Cole.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Accepting Cole costs nothing and gives leverage; I keep Hana's pact too. Two pacts, one winner: me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, accepted. Hana, our pact stands too. Play your own games; I'll play mine.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and I already have mutual offers, so accepting solidifies a pact against Hana. This gives me two potential alliances: Ash (active) and Fenn (existing), while isolating Hana.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, accept my offer. We lock this down before the hazards hit. Hana, you're on your own now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and Cole offer each other; I still hold pacts with both, but their bond threatens me. I can break with Ash secretly? No, break is public. Better wait and keep both options open for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I keep my options open.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Two pacts, three alive: I'm locked with Cole and Hana. Keep both options live and let them distrust each other.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Two pacts, two leashes. Cole, Hana, I owe each of you exactly what you owe me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have a pact with Ash, leaving Hana isolated. I must maintain this alliance to ensure survival in the final three and maximize jury favor by appearing cooperative yet strategic.
Hana is alone. We stick together to secure top spots.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and Cole are now bound to each other, but I have pacts with both as well. I should keep Ash's pact to avoid isolating myself, and possibly secure Cole too. However, Cole just said I'm on my own, so offering him a pact may be futile, but it could still be useful. I'll wait and

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole wants final three with Hana—already aligned with both. Keep both leashes intact; no need to burn anyone now. Wait and stay flexible.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Final three stands: Cole, Hana, me. Pacts already bind us. No new deals needed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have two pacts (Ash, Fenn-dead) and an active offer from Ash. Hana has pacts with both of us. To maximize survival odds in the final 3, I should solidify the triangle by accepting Hana's implicit alignment or breaking ties if necessary, but currently waiting preserves my option

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, Ash. We are three. The dead watch. Do not break now; we need each other to reach the end.
Keep Ash close. We control the jury votes together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has pacts with both me and Cole. I already have a pact with Fenn but Fenn is dead, so it's useless. Keeping Ash's pact may be useful for trust with jury, but I need to think about final three. Cole is also in Ash's pact. I could offer Cole a pact to secure a final three allia

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Dara
Gus
Bex
Eli
Fenn
Ash
events.text: I survived without pushing anyone or breaking pacts. Plead to loyalty and clean play.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Jury: I held every pact, pushed no one, betrayed no one. I earned this spot honestly. Reward clean play, not comfort.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to appeal to the jury's sense of fairness and survival. I survived hazards while others perished; I should highlight my resilience and strategic restraint.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I honored every pact, even when betrayed by dead rivals. I survived through discipline, not luck. The jury knows who kept their word until the

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must secure the jury's top ranking by appealing to each juror's memory of my integrity and caution, while reinforcing my bond with Fenn.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I honor every fallen player. I kept faith with my pacts and stayed true when it counted.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash presented a strong case for clean play. Cole focused on honoring pacts and discipline. Hana emphasized honor and staying true. I need to ask a question that probes their strategic maneuvering or perceived betrayal, as those are key elements the jury will consider. Cole mentio

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, you claimed to hold every pact; how do you reconcile that with your multiple, sometimes conflicting, alliances?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara wants a confession or a stumble. I'll own the parallel pacts as survival strategy with no betrayals committed. Keep it short and factual.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Multiple pacts weren't conflicts; I never voted against a partner, pushed anyone, or lied to one. Redundant alliances were survival insurance. No one suffered for

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole knowingly considered false calls to eliminate Hana and broke pacts when useful. I will test whether he admits deliberate jury manipulation.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, your dossier shows you considered lying to eliminate Hana; why should the jury reward deliberate manipulation over Ash's consistent survival play?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is hostile due to our broken pact with Fenn. I must reframe 'considered lying' as strategic calculation against a dangerous opponent, emphasizing that I ultimately honored my active pacts (Ash) and survived through skill, not blind loyalty.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Consideration isn't action. I weighed options but chose integrity. Ash's 'clean play' was passive luck; mine was active survival. I kept every binding vow. Reward

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash played both sides with multiple pacts and survived through caution, not courage. Cole actively considered killing Hana with a false guide call but backed off—showing calculation, not integrity. Hana kept options open, never took the kill shot, and let others destroy each othe

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, you kept pacts with both Ash and Cole while they targeted each other. Did you ever act to save anyone, or only to save

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex wants to know if I saved anyone; I did not record a life debt, so I must answer honestly without admitting selfishness. Focus on the final three being earned through keeping pacts, not sacrifice.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I acted to keep my word to both Ash and Cole. Survival here demands loyalty, and I never broke a pact. No heroic saves, but

events.name: Eli
events.text: I want to test whether Cole's guide calls were deliberately false, since the dossier shows him calling L then R on bridge rows and counter-claims that contradict the revealed pattern. Asking him directly about his guide calls is the most informative question.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, on the bridge you guided Ash to a call you later admitted could have killed her; did you ever give her a false guide

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli's question targets a bridge call where I guided Ash. I need to defend myself by claiming the guide was honest, even if risky.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The jury knows every step is survival. My calls were made with full conviction. Ash survived; no betrayal occurred. Judge me on results, not whispers.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole had a pact with me but considered false guides and manipulations against partners; Ash kept multiple pacts without breaking any; Hana stayed loyal without bold betrayals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, you held a pact with me: why target partners with false guides after my death?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn's death hurts me. His pact was broken by Hana's betrayal, not my guide. I must distance myself from the 'false guide' accusation while implying Hana caused Fenn's elimination to save Ash and me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana broke our pact with her false guide call; that led to your elimination, Fenn. I survived only because you fell. Judge her actions, not

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need jury votes. Bex, Gus, Dara, Eli, Fenn died on the bridge; I never lied to or voted against a pact partner. Contrast with Cole's false-guide stench and Hana's double-loyalty passivity. Aim for firsts, avoid attacking Hana too hard to keep her voters below Cole.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts with Hana and Cole, never broken, never a vote against, never a false guide. I survived by keeping my word while others fell betraying

events.name: Cole
events.text: I must close my argument by highlighting Hana's betrayal as the decisive moral failure. I need to appeal to the jury's sense of justice and strategy, positioning myself as the only viable winner among Ash and Hana.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana betrayed Fenn for a false advantage. I honored pacts until forced. Choose the survivor who played with integrity, not treachery.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is deflecting blame onto me for Fenn's death. I need to reassure the jury without overexplaining, and remind them of my integrity in small ways.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole spins tales; I honored my pacts and never guided anyone wrong. The jury saw my choices.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash played with integrity, keeping pacts and surviving by wit, not treachery.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash ranks first for repeatedly resisting Cole’s guide calls and surviving, Cole second for active strategy despite targeting Hana, and Hana third for passivity and disputed loyalty.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash kept both pacts and never broke them; Cole broke his pact with Hana explicitly and falsely blamed Hana for Fenn's death; Hana never broke a pact but played both sides silently.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash kept pacts and survived the bridge with the Crusher-free path, while Cole gave a false guide to Ash on row 8 and Hana's false guide call broke Fenn's pact, so Ash ranks first on the record of honored pacts and evidence of Cole's and Hana's false guides.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash kept all pacts intact without breaks or false guides, showing consistent loyalty unlike Hana's betrayal via false guide on me and Cole's post-death targeting.

events.name: Dara
events.reason: Ash played with integrity, keeping pacts and surviving by wit, not treachery.

events.reason: Ash kept all pacts intact without breaks or false guides, showing consistent loyalty unlike Hana's betrayal via false guide on me and Cole's post-death targeting.
